newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Ruling Socialists appeal against election verdict.
newsitem.headline: Ruling Socialists appeal against election verdict.

text.p: Serbian President Slobodan MIlosevic's Socialist Party has appealed against a ruling that awarded victory to opposition parties in elections in the city of Nis, a commission official said on Friday.

Mass protests erupted in Serbia after the ruling Socialists (SPS) annulled opposition election victories in 14 large Serbian towns, including Belgrade, last November on grounds of unspecified "irregularities".

Miroslav Rajkovic, an opposition member of the multi-party election commission in Nis, said the local SPS board had filed an appeal against a ruling by the commission last Tuesday that the opposition had fairly won the town.

He told Reuters by telephone that the SPS chairman of the commission gave no details of the appeal to the rest of the body, calling it "a private affair of the SPS". But the Nis municipal court was due to rule on the appeal on Saturday.
Almost nine straight weeks of demonstrations by the Zajedno (Together) coalition have rattled the foundations of effective one-party rule in Serbian-led federal Yugoslavia dating back to 1945.
